summary: Y2O3 thin films were deposited using cyclopentadienyl-type yttrium compounds and water as precursors via atomic layer deposition (ALD). The growth rate varied with temperature, and the films showed low impurity levels and good crystallinity. The study aimed to explore the use of cyclopentadienyl-type precursors for low-temperature ALD of Y2O3.
evidence: Y2O3 thin films were grown onto Si(100) substrates by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using organometallic precursors, viz. tris(cyclopentadienyl)yttrium, Cp3Y, and tris(methylcyclopentadienyl)yttrium, (CpCH3)3Y (Cp = cyclopentadienyl). Water was used as oxygen source. The deposition rate of yttria in the Cp3Y/H2O process slightly increased as a function of the deposition temperature, viz. from 1.5 to 1.8 Å/cycle at temperatures from 250 to 400 °C. With the (CpCH3)3Y/H2O process, a constant growth rate of 1.2-1.3 Å/cycle was achieved in a wide deposition temperature range of 200 -400 °C.
